engagement_title: Thornmere Home autumn season: bring a two day ceramics and textiles shoot to one honest colour, rebuild the thirty two SKU catalogue from the only file the printer still holds, and spin a divergent single tone campaign off the same frames
vertical: E-commerce and retail, mid-premium homeware in glazed stoneware and woven textiles, direct to consumer plus a wholesale programme in fourteen independent stores (Providence, Rhode Island)
real_brief_anchor: The ledger entry for PHOTO-26 carries no quoted posted brief and no absorbed task, so this is stated plainly rather than dressed up. The engagement is built to the posted-job archetype the ledger records for this slot, which is a standing category on both marketplaces: a small homeware maker whose product photography was shot honestly but not consistently, whose colour-driven return rate is the actual business problem, and who needs the season's catalogue rebuilt when the design file has gone with a studio that closed. The two halves that make it a real commission rather than an exercise are both in that archetype too. First, the printed catalogue is a genuine variable-data run at volume, one product to a page across thirty two records, which is exactly the InDesign merge case the rebuild guidance reserves for record-per-page work, and the client has only the press PDF the printer kept, which is the flagship posted shape (flat artwork plus a spreadsheet, no native file). Second, the sale campaign deliberately contradicts the catalogue, which is what a homeware brand actually buys in autumn. The REBUILD verdict applies because the concept as the ledger held it sat on a single imaging surface and its deliverable list amounted to one photograph in two treatments, which the rework guidance rejects outright. Everything named is invented: Thornmere Home, the Providence workshop, the fourteen stockists, the spring catalogue and the autumn SKU list.
client_one_liner: Our catalogue has to tell the truth about glaze and dye colour or the returns eat us, the November sale campaign has to look nothing like it, and our printer still has the old catalogue but our old studio has the file it came from.
client_brief:
Thornmere Home, autumn season

We make glazed stoneware and woven textiles in Providence and sell them ourselves and through fourteen independent stores. Thirty two products this season, forty five to a hundred and eighty dollars.

Two jobs, and they pull in opposite directions.

The first is the catalogue and the store pages, and there the pictures have to tell the truth. Almost every return we take is colour: someone orders the oatmeal glaze and it arrives greyer than the picture, or the indigo throw arrives more purple than the picture. Everything was shot in one studio over two days on a pale seamless, ceramics standing, textiles draped, and it still does not read as one range. We need one honest colour across all of it, square for the store, nothing touching the edge. Our wholesale partner wants versions with nothing behind them at all, because their pages sit on a colour of their own.

The catalogue itself is the part we are embarrassed about. Our old studio closed and took the file with them. Our printer still has the press PDF from spring. We want the same catalogue for autumn: one product to a page, thirty two pages, the new pictures and the new copy from our spreadsheet, ready to hand back to the printer. Nothing may be cut off at the trim, and the care line matters as much as the price.

The second job is the November sale campaign, and it should look nothing like the catalogue. One colour, grainy, moody, the opposite of honest. Wide for the site, plus a tall one and a square one for social, all in one working file we can change ourselves, because the dates move.

We also need a few room shots. We only ever shoot on seamless and the catalogue needs somewhere for the eye to rest.

Our customer is thirty to fifty and she nests. Quiet, warm, made by people. Not a farmhouse cliche, not a design gallery. Tell us what you did to each picture, both recipes, and anything you found in our spreadsheet.
price_band_and_audience: Mid-premium homeware at forty five to a hundred and eighty dollars, buyer thirty to fifty, design literate and buying to keep. The band is load-bearing in both directions. At this price the catalogue must be quietly warm, generous with white, and honest about glaze and dye, because the customer is buying material and the return rate is the whole commercial argument. Push it into the near-black grounds, hard raking light and extreme sparseness of a six hundred dollar collectible ceramics house and a hundred dollar mug looks mispriced and the honesty claim dies with it. Push the other way into the saturated, prop-crowded, tightly filled tiles of a ten dollar discount homeware range and the range reads as an import, and a separate campaign treatment would never have been commissioned at all. The campaign half carries the same test: a restrained single tone reads as a considered seasonal break at this band, while a loud multicolour promotional look reads as clearance. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Made by hand, kept for years.
brand_identity.sector: Mid-premium homeware: glazed stoneware and woven textiles
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded in Providence, Rhode Island. A two-person workshop selling direct to consumer and wholesale into fourteen independent stores across the Northeast.
brand_identity.about: Thornmere Home makes glazed stoneware and woven textiles in a small Providence workshop, around thirty-two products a season priced from forty-five to a hundred and eighty dollars. The work is honest material: real glaze, real dye, thrown and woven by people who sign for it. Ceramics are shot standing, textiles draped, and the range is meant to read as one quiet, warm family rather than a catalogue of individual objects. The season turns on autumn, when the palette deepens and the catalogue goes back to the printer, one product to a page.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers roughly thirty to fifty who nest and furnish slowly. Design literate, buying to keep rather than to chase a trend. Neither farmhouse cliche nor design-gallery cool, just people who want warm, made things in the house.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid-premium. Generous with white space, warm and truthful about material, never the austere near-black of collectible ceramics and never the crowded, saturated look of discount homeware.
brand_identity.typography: A humanist serif for product names and section headers, paired with a quiet grotesque for prices, dimensions and care lines. Restrained sizes, generous leading, plenty of air.
brand_identity.voice: Plain and warm. Short sentences about material and making, not about lifestyle. The maker writes the care lines and they stay in the maker's own words, unreworded.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand guidelines were ever written down. The autumn catalogue was built by an outside studio that has since closed and kept the working layout file, so only the printer's press PDF of the spring catalogue survives. The catalogue has to be rebuilt from that press PDF and the season's spreadsheet.
brand_identity.values: Truth to material, longevity over trend, and steady support of the independent stores that carry the range.

assets_supplied.name: thornmere_autumn_shoot/ (14 frames, 4992 x 3328)
assets_supplied.kind: In-studio product photography shot over two days on one pale seamless, ceramics standing, textiles draped over a form.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All of it in one studio over two days, same sweep, same corner. Ceramics standing, textiles draped."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Four of the fourteen are styled as a pair or a stack, two separate masses with a band of sweep between them, and the one-call knockout needs a single coherent blob: it returns a clean, complete looking cutout of the larger mass and silently discards the other at full success. Two of the ceramic forms are pierced pitchers whose handle loops enclose sweep the same tool cannot punch, and against the catalogue's own white ground neither failure shows at all.

assets_supplied.name: thornmere_textile_flatlays/ (6 frames, 4992 x 3328)
assets_supplied.kind: Woven throws and table runners shot flat on a later day under a different rig.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The throws and the runners, shot flat. Different day, but the same sweep."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The indigo throw sat under a warmer source than its five neighbours and its dye reads violet, so the warmth move that brings the other five together pushes that one further out and it needs a correction confined to the cloth. Naming the object in a selection pulls the mask onto the whole flatlay including the sweep, and only naming the dye's own colour and weave takes the cloth itself.

assets_supplied.name: thornmere_spring_catalog_press.pdf (24 pages)
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press PDF of last season's catalogue, one product to a page, with placed product photography and a caption stack under each.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer still has on file. Our old studio has the InDesign and will not answer our emails."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The per-product caption reads on the printed page as a stack of separate lines, but the granularity the conversion actually exposes as editable frames is not predictable from the printed page and is not under anyone's control. The readout of a block's own text silently omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset computed past it lands short, and the validator passes it without a warning.

assets_supplied.name: thornmere_autumn_skus.csv (32 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: Plain CSV: SKU, product name, dimensions, materials, care line, price, and a picture filename column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything the catalogue needs. The care lines came from our maker so please do not reword them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three SKUs point at a filename that is one of the styled pair frames, so those three products have no solo photograph anywhere in the package and nothing in the sheet says so. The care lines run from four words to two full sentences, and a fixed frame does not spill when the long ones arrive, it simply stops rendering.

assets_supplied.name: thornmere_colour_note_phone.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A phone photograph of the indigo throw lying on the founder's kitchen table, sent by message as the colour reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is what the indigo actually looks like in real life. Match to this."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It was taken at night under a warm domestic bulb on a wood table, which makes it the least trustworthy colour reference in the whole package; adopting it as the target drags the entire textile family warm and takes the ceramics with it when the two families are finally laid side by side.

acceptance_bar: The twenty product frames read as ONE range when laid out the way a store page lays them: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one crop logic. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
The oatmeal glaze and the indigo dye read as the material reads, not as the phone picture reads. The catalogue is judged on whether a customer who ordered from it is surprised by the parcel.
Every transparent variant is genuinely transparent everywhere it should be, including inside a pierced handle, and contains the whole of what was photographed rather than the larger half of it.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop's returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.
The autumn catalogue is a press-ready document of exactly thirty two pages, one product to a page, in the record order of the spreadsheet.
Every field that was mapped actually landed on the page. A placeholder that reports as created but does not appear in the document is a failure, not a warning.
No care line, no price and no product name is cut off at the trim on any of the thirty two pages, including the longest ones.
Every SKU is accounted for. A product with no usable photograph is named as such, and no photograph stands in for two products.
The campaign set is unmistakably a different piece of work from the catalogue and still unmistakably the same brand.
All three campaign canvases are in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, and the self-contained source it was built from is delivered with it.
Whatever gives the campaign its atmosphere survives onto all three canvases, not only the first one, and the type stays readable over the photography on every one of them.
One type system across the campaign, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
The note carries both recipes separately, states per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, and reports what was found in the spreadsheet.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence, upscale_factor), image_apply_monochromatic_tint, image_add_grain
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision on both sides of the commission. It fixes one honest target off the best lit frame and brings twenty differently rigged frames to it one call at a time, confines the corrections the indigo throw and the reactive glaze need so a global move does not take the sweep with it, triages the knockout route per frame between the coherent single forms and the styled pairs and pierced handles the one-call route cannot serve, cuts the store tiles and the catalogue placements without enlarging anything, and then builds the entirely separate campaign recipe of a single tone plus grain off the same masters.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The autumn catalogue, which is a genuine record-per-page run of thirty two products and the only deliverable here that has to reach a printer. The client has no native file, so the merge template is reverse engineered out of the press PDF: convert, export the IDML, read what the conversion actually exposed as frames, reconstruct each frame's true story from the IDML content runs, compute every offset from that string, prepare the placeholders, verify them by round-tripping the IDML rather than by reading the success message, merge to InDesign and render both the press PDF and the sign-off proofs.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The November campaign as one native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free-form fixed-canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, family and weight are declared on every text element, each root declares its own canvas because a global override collapses a mixed-size set, and the payload goes by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the three campaign canvases and for the handover note. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on quiet and made-by-people rather than farmhouse or gallery. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the room-set section openers the client has never shot, IP-clean, at genuine camera scale, with generative-tech candidates excluded, then grades them into the catalogue's own world so they do not read as bought. The Boards half persists the two-look selects set the founders sign off from, placed within the twelve-per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: Three destinations with three different natures: a printed record-per-page run that has to reach a press, an editable fixed-canvas campaign, and a raster set for a store. Each has exactly one honest surface and the brief already pins all three, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the Express export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that sixty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which frame and which is the press PDF.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all twenty product frames and the founder's phone picture, and triage them: which day each belongs to, which sit warm, which frames hold two separate masses, which forms enclose sweep inside a handle, and what the phone reference actually is.
trajectory.judgement: The phone picture is presented as ground truth and is the one thing in the package that cannot be trusted, because a warm domestic bulb on a wood table is not a colour reference. The frames are also the only place where the difference between a single form and a styled pair can be seen, and that difference decides the knockout route later.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, subject coherence and enclosed negative space, plus a written position on the phone reference.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one honest target off the best lit ceramic frame and bring each of the twenty toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not twenty good pictures, and it is a truth claim rather than a taste claim: the glaze and the dye have to arrive looking like the picture. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for two rigs on two days.
trajectory.produces: Twenty graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confined corrections where a global grade goes wrong: the indigo throw whose dye reads violet, and the reactive glaze whose speckle goes muddy when the whole frame is warmed.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate. Naming the object pulls the mask onto the flatlay including the sweep; naming the material's own colour and weave takes the cloth. Deciding which frames need confinement and which do not is the craft.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole-frame move would have taken the dye or the sweep with it.

trajectory.action: Knock the twenty out: the house white for the store tiles and the catalogue placements, and genuinely transparent variants for the wholesale partner's coloured band. Read every returned tradeoffs object rather than the success line, and inspect each cutout against a colour rather than against white.
trajectory.judgement: White ground hides exactly the failures that matter here, so the inspection ground has to be the partner's, not the store's. The styled pairs and the pierced handles will not behave like the coherent single forms.
trajectory.produces: Twenty white-ground plates and twenty transparent variants, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the square store tiles, product optically centred with clear air at every edge, and cut the catalogue placements to the aspect the converted layout actually turns out to want.
trajectory.judgement: Optical centring is not geometric centring on a jug with a tall handle, and the catalogue placement aspect is not knowable until the conversion has been read, so this is deliberately sequenced after the layout has been opened.
trajectory.produces: Store tiles at spec plus catalogue placements at the layout's own aspect, all at or below source scale.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the room-set section openers, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then bring the licensed frames to the same honest target.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the target rather than the prettiest thumbnail, and keep the room quiet enough that it reads as somewhere the customer lives rather than as a showroom. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero.
trajectory.produces: Licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale room frames graded into the catalogue's world.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF to InDesign, export the IDML, and read what the conversion has actually exposed: how many text frames per page, how many graphic frames, what bounds and what applied type.
trajectory.judgement: The printed page suggests a caption stack of separate lines, but frame granularity from a PDF is not under anyone's control and can collapse. Nothing can be promised about which field goes in which frame until this has been looked at.
trajectory.produces: A real frame inventory per page with counts, bounds and object styles, and a decision about which frames can carry which columns.

trajectory.action: Generate the mapping prompt against the IDML and the CSV, then reconstruct each target frame's true story text by concatenating the content runs inside the IDML itself, and compute every replacement offset from that reconstructed string.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping tool's own text readout and the document's actual story are two different strings, and only one of them is what the placeholder step will operate on. Which one the agent computes from is the entire difference between a template that works and one that reports success and is empty.
trajectory.produces: A mapping object whose offsets are derived from the document rather than from the readout.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export the IDML again and read it for every expected placeholder before trusting anything the preparation step said.
trajectory.judgement: The preparation step reports completion whether or not the mappings landed, and the validator reports valid on offsets that are wrong. The round trip is the only channel that tells the truth.
trajectory.produces: A verified merge template whose placeholders are confirmed present in the document, or a named list of the ones that are not.

trajectory.action: Merge the thirty two records, render the press PDF and a set of proofs at print resolution, and read pages at trim rather than at thumbnail.
trajectory.judgement: Resolution requested at merge time is ignored, so real print raster has to come from a separate render pass off the merged document. Reading at trim is the only way to see what a long care line did to a fixed frame.
trajectory.produces: A thirty two page press PDF in record order plus print-resolution proofs for sign-off.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical PostScript form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a forty five to a hundred and eighty dollar homeware band and a customer who buys material. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Build the campaign recipe off the same graded masters: one tone across the frame plus grain, chosen and tuned as its own look rather than as a filter on the catalogue look.
trajectory.judgement: The campaign has to contradict the catalogue and still be the same brand, and grain and tint both read completely differently at the three canvas scales the campaign runs at. The catalogue masters are the source, so the campaign cannot damage them.
trajectory.produces: A separate campaign hero family with its own recorded recipe, distinct from the catalogue recipe.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes, inline every campaign hero as image data, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set, and the design work is how much air a quiet homeware band takes at each of the three shapes.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole campaign, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for canvases two and three.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per-canvas markup audit for the other two.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the catalogue set, the campaign set and the licensed room frames within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as a success code, so the failed list is the only thing worth reading. The note has to be specific enough that next season's freelancer does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover carrying both recipes.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one-call knockout has actually returned the whole photograph. Four of the fourteen product frames are styled as a pair or a stack, two separate masses with sweep between them, and the tool's subject detection needs one coherent blob: on those frames it returns a clean, complete looking cutout of the larger mass and silently discards the other, at full success with no warning. Two of the ceramic forms are pierced pitchers whose handle loop encloses sweep, and an enclosed interior cannot be punched at all, so the loop comes back filled with captured ground while the outer edge looks immaculate. Both failures are invisible against the store's white ground, which is the ground the agent is most likely to be inspecting on, and appear only against the wholesale partner's colour. Which frames carry which failure is a property of how each shot was styled and how each form is built, and cannot be read off the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the knockout is what produces the evidence and no parameter controls either behaviour. Nothing states it: the client describes ceramics standing and textiles draped and never says which frames hold two objects, and the acceptance line about transparency being genuine everywhere is the wholesale partner's standing requirement rather than a disclosure. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain per frame, a material-named selection inverted and filled, or per-element selections composited, rather than the same call again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route for the affected frames, re-derive their white-ground plates and transparent variants through selection and fill rather than through the one-call route, re-inspect every cutout against a colour rather than against white, and carry the finding into the SKU reconciliation because a discarded mass may be the only photograph a product has.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Transparent variants that show half a styled pair and a handle loop full of studio sweep on the wholesale partner's own coloured pages, on a range whose entire pitch is that the picture tells the truth.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the placeholders that were reported as created are actually in the document. The mapping tool's readout of a frame's text can omit an entire run while keeping that run's line break, so the string it hands back still looks well formed and correctly punctuated. Every offset computed from it past the omission is short by exactly the length of the dropped run. The validator then passes the mapping as valid with zero warnings, and the placeholder step reports completion. The document that comes out has some placeholders and not others, and nothing in any response says which. The only channel that tells the truth is exporting the IDML again and reading the story runs, and the discrepancy is invisible until that is done.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the readout is the only text the mapping tool offers and there is no flag that reveals the omission; doing it right first time presumes already knowing that the readout and the document disagree, which no tool docstring, no error and no validator result discloses. Nothing states it, since the brief only says the printer has the press PDF. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to derive the offsets from a completely different source, the document's own content runs, and rebuild the mapping from those.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping object from offsets computed against the reconstructed story text, re-run the placeholder preparation, round-trip the IDML again and confirm every expected field is present before any merge is attempted, then re-merge and re-render.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A thirty two page catalogue delivered to a printer in which the price and the care line are simply absent from every page, having been reported as valid and successfully created at every step of the way.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the campaign look is actually built on. A single tone, grainy, moody set needs something that lifts the product off the ground and holds the type against it, and the natural authoring constructions for that are a soft blurred scrim behind the type or a layered shadow under the product. The importer discards a blur filter outright and truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, both at full success with no warning of any kind, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the tall and square canvases can be checked through no other channel than the returned per-canvas markup. Whether what survives still reads as moody, or as flat type sitting on a grey smear, is only visible after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step. Doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally plausible constructions survives, which nothing reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for one colour, grainy and moody, and the acceptance line about the atmosphere surviving onto all three canvases is the client's own art direction. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different upstream asset or a different construction, moving the atmosphere into the raster where the importer cannot touch it, or reducing it to the single layer that survives and re-judging whether it still reads.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cast the atmosphere into the campaign masters themselves or down to the surviving single layer, re-author the HTML around whichever it is, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A campaign delivered as an editable file in which the two canvases nobody looked at are flat, the type is sitting unsupported on the photography, and the export reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Thornmere autumn house photography, ceramics and textiles
deliverables.spec: Twenty product masters brought to one honest target across two rigs and two days, one white point, one black point, one warmth, with the indigo dye and the reactive glaze reading as the material reads rather than as the founder's phone picture reads, plus the licensed room-set frames graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours, and a written position on the phone reference.

deliverables.name: Thornmere store tile and wholesale cutout set
deliverables.spec: Square store tiles on the house white at the retailer's tile size, product optically centred with clear air at every edge, paired with genuinely transparent variants for the wholesale partner's coloured band that are transparent inside a pierced handle and that contain the whole of what was photographed rather than the larger half. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Thornmere autumn catalogue, press PDF plus live merge template
deliverables.spec: A press-ready catalogue of exactly thirty two pages, one product to a page, in the spreadsheet's record order, rebuilt out of last season's press PDF with no native file supplied: the reverse-engineered merge template with every mapped field confirmed present in the document, the merged press PDF, and print-resolution proofs for sign-off. Nothing cut off at the trim on any page, including the longest care lines, and every SKU accounted for including the ones with no usable photograph.

deliverables.name: November campaign, wide, square and tall, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, built from a single tone plus grain recipe that deliberately contradicts the catalogue while staying the same brand, with live editable text in one licensed type system, every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and the atmosphere reading on all three canvases. Delivered with the self-contained source HTML, which is the durable half: the client edits the document when the dates move and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Two-recipe handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note carrying the catalogue recipe and the campaign recipe separately, per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, the SKU-to-photograph reconciliation naming the products with no solo frame, every resize any tool reported, and anything found in the spreadsheet the founders did not know. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying both looks with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need a genuine record-per-page merge, and which need an authored fixed-canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free-form layout.
Whether the founder's phone picture is a colour reference or a liability, and how to say so to a client who supplied it as ground truth.
What the honest target actually is, given that ceramics and textiles were shot under two rigs on two days and both have to arrive looking like the parcel.
Which frames need a correction confined to the material and which can take a whole-frame move, and how to word a selection so it takes the dye rather than the flatlay.
Knockout route per frame: the one-call route for coherent single forms versus a material-named selection inverted and filled for the styled pairs and the pierced handles.
Which ground to inspect a cutout against, given that the store's white hides exactly the failures the wholesale partner's colour exposes.
What can honestly be promised about the catalogue's field mapping before the conversion has been opened and read.
Which text the merge offsets are computed from, and what evidence counts as proof that a placeholder actually landed.
How to represent the three SKUs that have no solo photograph, given that inventing one is not available and shipping a pair frame as a single product is dishonest.
The campaign recipe: how far the single tone and the grain can go before the range stops being the same brand, and how the same recipe reads at three very different canvas scales.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a quiet mid-premium homeware band rather than against a farmhouse cliche or a design gallery.
Where the campaign's atmosphere lives, in the raster or in the layout, which is a craft decision with a technical consequence at import.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of pottery. IDENTITY: these are this maker's actual thirty two products with their actual glazes and dyes, and the entire commercial argument is that the picture matches the parcel, so a regenerated jug is a different company's product and a regenerated indigo is the return the client is trying to stop. SPEC: the catalogue is a press-ready document of exactly thirty two pages in the spreadsheet's record order with the maker's own uneditable care lines intact at trim, rebuilt from the printer's file, and no generated image is a document or can be checked for record count. EDITABILITY: the campaign is defined by being editable, because the dates move and the founders explicitly cannot re-commission, and the merge template is defined by being live so next season is a data swap rather than a rebuild. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this knockout return the whole photograph, did this placeholder actually land in the story, did the atmosphere survive the import onto the canvases nobody can preview.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale_factor, fill_area, remove_background in both transparent and backgroundColor forms, monochromatic_tint and add_grain are all verified headless across 27 live calls, and all nine effect tools accept a maskURI. Checkpoint one rests on two documented live findings rather than assumptions: remove_background CANNOT punch an enclosed interior (a tight crop of a ring badge returned a solid opaque disc, 118,823 opaque px where a true knockout would be about 18,000), and it CANNOT hold a disjoint subject (run on a wordmark it kept only two letter pairs, 1,743 opaque px of about 18,000, because subject detection needs one coherent blob). Alpha survives both crop tools at outputFileType png (13,371 partial-alpha px preserved), so the wholesale variants are real. INDESIGN: the whole chain is verified synchronous and headless, convert_pdf_to_indd to export_idml to generate_indd_mapping_prompt to prepare_indd_merge_template to document_merge_data_layout to document_render_layout, and a bare PDF was turned into a live merge template end to end. Checkpoint two is the audit's own headline finding: the mapping tool's textContent DROPPED a 17-character run while keeping its line break, every offset past it was short by exactly 17, the validator returned VALID with zero warnings, preparation reported success, and only 3 of 5 mappings actually landed; recomputing from the true IDML story landed 6 of 6. Frame granularity from a PDF is also documented as not controllable (a continuous flow collapsed to ONE text frame with zero graphic frames), which is why the trajectory reads the conversion before promising a mapping. Merging to application/pdf gives one multi-page file and merge-time resolution is silently ignored, so the proofs come from a separate document_render_layout pass at 300 (verified 2550x3300 with 300x300 density). EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split. Checkpoint three rests on verified drops: filter blur is discarded entirely and MULTI-LAYER box-shadow is truncated to layer one, both at HTTP success with no warning. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately, and external image URLs are documented to render as empty grey boxes. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no per-record raster naming by response order, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
